source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Use Ireasoning MIB browser professional:
1. Enable SNMP v3 agent settings from WEB UI. (Refer to WebGUI spec/user guide).
2. Enable the corresponding user account SNMPv3 settings at WEB UI.
3. Open Ireasoning MIB browser, load the MIB files.
4. Setup the settings of MIB browser to access BMC according to the WEB UI SNMPv3 settings.
5. Left-click on the $target and expand subtree.
6. Right-Click on the node and use "Get Next" or "Get Subtree" to get all the values of the $target.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
Use NetSNMP to check.
1. Enable SNMP v3 agent settings from WEB UI. (Refer to WebGUI spec/user guide).
2. Enable the corresponding user account SNMPv3 settings at WEB UI.
3. Put the mib files into the netsnmp search path.
http://www.net-snmp.org/docs/FAQ.html#Where_should_I_put_my_MIB_files_
4. Use NetSNMP "get type" of command(s) to retrieve the values of the $target from BMC.

deepseek_columns.ai_packages_needed: snmpwalk (net-snmp), BMC SNMP agent must be enabled + community configured
deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- SNMP "monitor_leds" monitoring reads specific BMC MIB data via the SNMP agent; from a 2nd management host run `snmpwalk -v2c -c ${SNMP_COMMUNITY:?operator must set SNMP community (v2c) or v3 creds} "$BMC_IP" .1.3.6.1.4.1.8072.2.3.2.1.2 | grep -i leds (or walk the vendor MIB subtree once the SNMP community/v3 creds + MIB are configured). Enable + point SNMP agent first.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return FULL snmpwalk output for the LED OID subtree so the user confirms the monitor_leds SNMP data is correct.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: SNMP queries need a management host + enabled/configured SNMP agent on the BMC (community/v3 + firewall); enabling SNMP is a config change, and some BMC SNMP sets expose credentials - use read-only community.

historical_reviews.gpt_v2: BLOCKED / CHANGED; correctly separates telemetry from physical indication/control but overstates supplyable Project LED mapping as a permanent block.

original_test_intent: Retrieve the platform-defined LED indicator telemetry over SNMPv3 and verify each in-scope indicator's physical identity, encoded color/state/blink condition and asserted meaning against the Project-approved chassis state, with any physical visual correlation kept as a separate checkpoint.
original_method: An engineer enables an SNMPv3 account in WebUI and uses IReasoning MIB Browser Get Next/Get Subtree on undefined `$target`; Criteria switch to Net-SNMP without defining LED objects or acceptance states.
manual_activity: An engineer must configure SNMPv3, approve the LED identity/encoding and expected chassis-state matrix, and provide timestamped visual evidence if physical illumination is in scope. The agent can perform the bounded telemetry read and correlation.
required_inputs: vendor MIB module/version and exact LED telemetry OIDs
index-to-location and purpose map for system, fault, identify, power, drive, network or other indicators
type, color, state, blink-pattern and asserted-condition enum semantics
declared chassis/fault/identify/power state and expected values
decision whether physical visual behavior is required and whether a safe stimulus already exists
least-privilege SNMPv3 profile and manager ACL
approved client equivalence and cleanup policy
safety_requirements: Keep this review's executable core read-only: never issue SNMP SET, identify-control, fault injection, LED override or unrelated component action.
Do not clear or mask a genuine fault/identify indication merely to create an expected baseline.
Do not use v2c, the generic `.1.3.6.1.4.1.8072...` example or grep-only/empty output as LED evidence.
Map enum values to exact indicator identity and declared system condition; a returned value alone cannot prove physical illumination.
Protect SNMPv3 secrets and stop on a write-capable object, unexpected asserted fault, unknown encoding or BMC instability; do not auto-retry.
Restore temporary SNMPv3 setup and verify no LED, fault, identify or power state was changed or left asserted.
agent_execution_scope: After engineer setup, query exact approved LED telemetry objects over bounded SNMPv3 GET/GETNEXT/WALK and retain typed index/enum/timestamp evidence.
Compare telemetry with the declared chassis condition and correlate with separately supplied visual evidence only when physical coverage is required.
Do not operate WebUI, control an LED, inject a fault, claim visual success from telemetry, claim IReasoning coverage when only Net-SNMP ran or issue a DUT verdict.
engineer_actions: Approve the indicator object/index/location/purpose and state-encoding matrix plus expected baseline.
Define whether visual behavior or a safe pre-existing stimulus is in scope, capture any physical evidence, configure/restore SNMPv3 and approve tool equivalence.
Investigate unexpected real fault/identify states and issue PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The command uses the wrong security mode and an unrelated demonstration OID; a text filter cannot prove indicator identity, enum meaning, blink semantics or physical behavior.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use exact vendor-MIB SNMPv3 LED telemetry objects with full typed index/enum output under a declared chassis state; keep physical observation and any control/stimulus as explicit separate checkpoints.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: IReasoning, SNMPv3 WebUI/account setup, undefined `$target`, Net-SNMP Criteria and 10/5-minute values remain preserved source evidence.

modernized_recommendation.status: PROJECT LED OBJECT AND STATE MATRIX REQUIRED
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Map each telemetry row to a physical indicator location/purpose and its color/state/blink enums, collect bounded SNMPv3 values under a recorded chassis condition, compare with the expected matrix, and correlate an independently timestamped photograph only where visual coverage is required.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The identified chassis, LED board/backplane population, BMC firmware and matching vendor MIB.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Vendor LED/indicator MIB and chassis indicator behavior specification plus Project state matrix.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds physical indicator identity, enum and asserted-condition semantics and separates protocol telemetry from physical illumination and control coverage.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Net-SNMP may prove equivalent object values when approved but not IReasoning UI; SNMP telemetry cannot alone prove color, brightness or blinking at the physical LED.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Indicator OIDs/indexes/map, expected chassis state, visual scope, reference and client decision.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Telemetry can lag or abstract hardware indicators, and a photograph without timestamp/state identity cannot prove correlation.

project_override_considerations: Project SPEC may select the indicator set, require or omit physical visual correlation and approve Net-SNMP instead of IReasoning, but must record original/actual tool, object-level equivalence, untested visual/control coverage and the exact chassis condition. Read-only telemetry cannot be claimed as LED-control validation.
expected_evidence: approved LED index-to-location/purpose and color/state/blink/asserted-condition map
redacted SNMPv3 WebUI/account/ACL configuration and cleanup artifacts
vendor MIB identity with exact numeric OID/type/index/enum mapping
declared chassis/fault/identify/power state and complete bounded typed telemetry
timestamped physical photo or observation mapped to the same indicator/state when required
proof no LED/fault/identify/power control changed, tool/coverage statement, health logs and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure requires IReasoning/SNMPv3 while Criteria changes to Net-SNMP, `$target` and LED state acceptance are unresolved, and DeepSeek changes to v2c plus an unrelated generic subtree. The read-only indicator-monitoring purpose remains identifiable.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Indicator objects, state enums, expected chassis condition and visual scope are Project execution-readiness inputs for a clear read-only monitoring purpose. Once supplied and manually configured, telemetry collection is automatable and visual correlation can remain engineer-owned; permanent BLOCKED is not justified.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Retains hybrid execution but rejects the v2c/generic OID and adds exact indicator identity, enum, state and telemetry-versus-visual boundaries.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Changes BLOCKED to REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION under ED-36 while preserving hard stops against guessing state encodings or issuing controls.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Independently confirms the classification and strengthens the separation among telemetry, physical observation and control/fault-stimulus coverage.

review_improvement: Prevents an SNMP response from being misreported as proof of physical LED behavior and prevents an unapproved control or fault injection from being substituted for the source's monitoring intent.
independent_technical_reasoning: LED telemetry, physical illumination and LED-control behavior are different coverage domains. The source clearly asks to monitor through SNMP, while exact identity and enum data can be supplied by the Project. Therefore manual setup plus bounded read and any optional human visual checkpoint fits REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION, not permanent BLOCKED.
